newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota denies report of third Brazil plant.
newsitem.headline: Toyota denies report of third Brazil plant.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp on Thursday denied media reports in Brazil that it will build a third plant in Brazil to produce cars.

Several Brazilian dailies reported on Wednesday that Toyota is planning to build a third factory in Brazil to make its Starlet car by the year 2000. The reports said the plant was likely to be built adjacent to its second plant near Sao Paulo.
"The reports were speculation. We have no such plans," a Toyota spokesman told Reuters.

Toyota is now building the second plant in Indaiatuba, about 80 km northwest of Sao Paulo, to start production of Corolla subcompact cars by the end of 1998 at an annual rate of 15,000 units, the spokesman added.

A mission of the Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren), led by its chairman Shoichiro Toyoda, who is also Toyota's chairman, is visiting Brazil, Chile and Argentina. The trip began on March 18 and ends on March 29.

Toyota assembles the Bandeirante heavy sport-utility vehicle (called the Land Cruiser in Japan) at its first plant near Sao Paulo with an annual output rate of more than 3,000 units, the spokesman said.
